sections.html: Otocinclus vestitus can be easily identified by the typical pattern in the caudal fin. The species name vestitus is Latin and means "dressed".

Family: Loricariidae. Size: 3.5 cm. Temperature: 25–30°C. pH: 6.0–7.5.

IUCN Red List: despite the little information available on this species, it has a wide distribution and no apparent threats. Therefore, it is rated as Least Concern (IUCN 2023).
Otocinclus vestitus has a very large distribution. It is found in Peru, Bolivia, and Paraguay.
South America: Bolivia, Dept. Beni, Madeira basin. Peru, Rio Ampyiacu. Paraguay, Paraná basin.

Keeping O. vestitus is very easy; it is a typical beginner's species. Lovers of well planted aquaria enjoy it very much, as it is a perfect algae eater that feeds on the algae from the top of the leaves without hurting them at all.
This is a small group of Loricariids which do well in aquaria and will keep the algae down without harming the plants in the tank. Best kept in a group with more males for breeding purposes.
It feeds on algae from the top of leaves.
Omnivore: algae, tablet foods, flake and small frozen foods.
Breeding is very easy. For breeding a species-specific tank should be used. Technically speaking, breeding is very much like that of Corydoras species.
The females lay eggs on the plants and tank glass after the females have been chased around the tank by the male. Like Corydoras they present a t-position breeding mode.

Among the O. vestitus received from Paraguay was one very unusual xanthoristic specimen. Xanthorism is a mutation in which the cells with yellow pigment increase. It is a very rare occasion that such a conspicuous animal survives in the wild and grows to adult size. Old trade name: O. arnoldi.

They can be told apart from other Otocinclus spp. by the design on the caudal fin. There is a small spot on the caudal peduncle which is bordered by a light zone. There are also two bands in the caudal fin.

Etymology: the specific name vestitus is Latin for clothing, dress or attire; the allusion is not explained, perhaps referring to the several series of plates covering the body.

Otocinclus vestitus is the type species of the genus and as of 2021 there are 20 described species. More information can be found in the Catfish Atlas Volume 1.
